observations: OpenDHT defines HASH_LEN as 20 and InfoHash as Hash<20>, so its native application key width is exactly 160 bits.

Hash<20> has a direct constructor from a byte pointer plus length and a direct constructor from hexadecimal text; those constructors copy/parse the first 20 bytes or 40 hex digits rather than hashing them.
Hash::get(...) is a separate helper that hashes supplied data, so an extra hashing step is optional rather than mandatory when a caller already has the exact 20-byte Git SHA-1.
Dht::get takes const InfoHash& key directly, so the C++ retrieval API accepts the caller-constructed exact 160-bit key without an external namespace mapping layer.
OpenDHT Value carries a Blob data field and constructors from raw bytes; returned values therefore expose payload bytes to the caller for local verification in principle.

OpenDHT's generic Value size is capped at 64 KiB and default value expiration is 10 minutes, constraining any generic direct-object bridge and making durable independently pre-existing residency especially nontrivial.
No passive network lookup was issued, no canonical Git object bytes were retrieved, and no independently pre-existing target residency under the exact Git SHA-1 key was established in this slice.
probe.inference: OpenDHT passes the source-level exact native key-width/binding test in its C++ API: a raw 20-byte Git SHA-1 can be constructed directly as InfoHash and supplied to get without mandatory rehashing. Returned Value payload bytes can be inspected and locally Git-hash verified if they are the canonical Git object representation. The complete Phase-1 bridge remains unproven because no independently pre-existing target residency or canonical target bytes were observed, and the 64 KiB value ceiling limits generic direct-object coverage.

assumptions_uncertainty_residuals.assumption: The caller uses the direct InfoHash byte/hex constructor rather than InfoHash::get(...), which intentionally hashes its input.

frontier: OpenDHT InfoHash is exactly 20 bytes and can be constructed directly from raw bytes or 40 hex digits without mandatory hashing.
OpenDHT get(const InfoHash&) accepts that exact caller-supplied key; InfoHash::get is only an optional hashing helper.
Returned Value objects expose arbitrary payload bytes, allowing local Git hash verification in principle if canonical object bytes are actually present.

Independently pre-existing target residency and canonical target-byte retrieval remain unproven; generic direct-object coverage is additionally constrained by the 64 KiB Value ceiling and default 10-minute expiration.
